common.applies_to: Established bush rose (Hybrid Tea, Floribunda, provisional Grandiflora); dormant pruning
common.preserved_uncertainty: Only one source puts a number on a weak cane (10 mm for canes kept), so Pip uses no number (AF-5, as corrected). Why canes become weak is thinly evidenced (AF-2, Low). The twiggy and thorn-colour cues rest on one page each and are not shown (AF-6, AF-11). No source describes weak canes as arching or flopping (U-2).

content.look_for: Let's look for weak canes — thinner than a pencil — and at whether the middle of the bush is crowded.

criteria.text: A cane thinner than about a pencil may be weak.
Crowded: the bush is densely packed rather than open in the middle.

content.photo_limit: Thickness is hard to judge from a photo unless something of known size, such as a coin or pencil, is beside the cane. One angle can miss crowding at the back of the bush.
content.confirm_question: Check the cane against a pencil, and look at the middle of the bush from more than one side. Is it weak, or is the bush crowded?
content.not_sure_guidance: Take a photo with a coin or pencil beside the cane, or look at the middle from another side, then check again.
content.any_more_question: Can you see any more weak canes?
